- **Problém:** `start.js` importoval `PricingForm` z `./pricing`, což je celá stránka včetně Header a Footer.
- **Řešení:** Přidána komponenta `BodyMetricsForm` a použití ve `start.js` i `pricing.js`.

### 2. **Chybějící framer-motion**
- **Problém:** `start.js` používal `framer-motion` bez odpovídající závislosti v `package.json`.
- **Řešení:** Framer-motion odstraněn, animace přepsány na čisté CSS (`@keyframes startFadeIn`).

### 3. **Supabase API – getUserByEmail**
- **Problém:** Metoda `getUserByEmail` nemusí být dostupná ve všech verzích.
- **Řešení:** Přidán fallback:
  - pokus o `getUserByEmail`, pokud existuje;
  - jinak použití `listUsers` a filtrování podle emailu;
  - při chybě „user already exists“ nový pokus o nalezení uživatele.

### 4. **Index – hardcoded URL**
- **Problém:** Odkaz `https://app.bodyandmindon.cz/pricing`.
- **Řešení:** Nahrazen za `<Link href="/start">` pro lokální routing.

### 5. **API sessions – odpovědi**
- **Problém:** Střídání `res.send()` a `res.json()`.
- **Řešení:** Odpovědi standardizovány na `res.json()`.

### 6. **Onboarding stránka**
- **Problém:** Formulář bez emailu a jména, přímý insert do DB, bez API a bez generování plánu.
- **Řešení:** Stránka přesměrovává na `/start` (včetně query parametru `plan`).

## Nové a upravené soubory

| Soubor | Změna |
|--------|-------|
| `components/BodyMetricsForm.js` | Nová sdílená komponenta formuláře |
| `pages/pricing.js` | Používá `BodyMetricsForm` místo vlastního formuláře |
| `pages/start.js` | Používá `BodyMetricsForm`, odstraněn framer-motion |
| `pages/api/body-metrics.js` | Fallback pro `getUserByEmail` |
| `pages/api/sessions.js` | Jednotné JSON odpovědi |
| `pages/index.js` | Relativní odkazy přes `Link` |
| `pages/onboarding.js` | Přesměrování na `/start` |

## Provedené změny

### 1. Povinný e-mail pro registraci
- E-mail je teď povinný (HTML `required` + upravený popis)
- Bez e-mailu se uživatel nevyregistruje

### 2. Zpětná vazba po odeslání formuláře
- Úspěšná zpráva informuje o registraci
- Odkaz „Přihlásit se do profilu“ vede na `/login`

### 3. Stránka profilu (dashboard)
- Nová stránka `/dashboard`
- Po přihlášení se zobrazí:
  - údaje o uživateli (e-mail, jméno)
  - uložené metriky (váha, výška, cíl)
  - vygenerované plány (typ, kalorie, makra)
- Tlačítko „Odhlásit se“

### 4. API endpoint `/api/profile`
- Vrací data přihlášeného uživatele
- Vyžaduje platný JWT v hlavičce `Authorization`

### 5. Úpravy přihlášení
- Podpora parametru `?redirect=` v URL
- Po přihlášení přes magic link přesměrování na `/dashboard`

### 6. Navigace
- V hlavičce je nový odkaz „Profil“ na `/dashboard`

## Uživatelský tok

```
1. /start – vyplnění formuláře (e-mail povinný)
2. API vytvoří účet v Supabase Auth
3. Zpráva: „Registrace proběhla úspěšně…“ + odkaz „Přihlásit se do profilu“
4. /login – zadání e-mailu → odeslání magic linku
5. Kliknutí na odkaz v e-mailu → přesměrování na /dashboard
6. /dashboard – profil s metrikami a plány
```

**Důležité:** V Supabase Dashboard (Authentication → URL Configuration) nastavte „Redirect URLs“ na `https://app.bodyandmindon.cz/dashboard` (nebo vaši doménu), aby magic link fungoval.

<think><details><summary>Thought Process</summary>

The build is failing on Vercel because during the "Collecting page data" phase, Next.js tries to execute the login page (and possibly other pages that import supabaseClient). The supabaseClient.js creates the Supabase client at module load time, and when the URL or anon key are missing (they're not available during build on Vercel, or not set in the build environment), it throws "supabaseUrl is required."

The fix is to make the Supabase client creation resilient to missing env vars during build time - we should create the client only when the env vars are present, and export a client that might be null or a dummy, so that the build doesn't fail. Then at runtime on Vercel, the env vars will be available and the client will work.

Let me check the supabaseClient.js - it currently does:
```
if (!supabaseUrl || !supabaseAnonKey) {
  console.warn('Missing Supabase ENV...');
}
export const supabase = createClient(supabaseUrl, supabaseAnonKey);
```

So even when the vars are missing, it still calls createClient(undefined, undefined) which throws. We need to either:
1. Pass dummy values when env is missing so createClient doesn't throw during build
2. Or lazily create the client only when the variables are available

The cleanest approach for Next.js build is to create the client only when we have valid URL and key. _**User**_

Verify these issues exist and fix them:

Bug 1:
The function `generatePlanForEmail` has conflicting signatures on lines 13 and 148. Line 13 exports a version expecting `(email, isNewUser)`, while line 148 defines a version expecting only `(email)`. The API calls the function with an object as the second parameter on line 191 (`await generatePlanForEmail(payload.email, {...})`), causing a type mismatch. Additionally, line 205 incorrectly accesses `arguments[1]` instead of the proper function parameter, which will cause incorrect behavior.

Bug 2:
The code falls back to placeholder strings (`https://placeholder.supabase.co`, `placeholder-anon-key`) when environment variables are missing. This causes the Supabase client to initialize with invalid credentials, allowing the application to appear to start successfully but fail at runtime when any database query executes. Production deployments missing these environment variables will crash silently without proper warnings, making debugging difficult.

 @lib/generatePlan.js:12-13 @lib/generatePlan.js:147-148 @pages/api/body-metrics.js:170-171 @lib/supabaseClient.js:3-5

---

## Bug 1 – `generatePlanForEmail`

**Stav:** Opraveno.

- **`lib/generatePlan.js`**  
  - Jediná definice je na řádcích 143–224:  
    `async function generatePlanForEmail(email, options = {})`.  
  - Druhý parametr je vždy objekt `options`, nikde se nepoužívá `arguments[1]`.  
  - Na ř. 178: `const opts = typeof options === 'object' ? options : {}`.  
  - Na ř. 209–216: `sendOpts` se skládá z `opts.loginPassword`, `opts.loginUrl` atd. a předává se do `sendPlanEmail(email, planHtml, sendOpts)`.

- **`pages/api/body-metrics.js`** (ř. 86–91)  
  Volá se správně s objektem jako druhým argumentem:
  ```js
  planResult = await generatePlanForEmail(payload.email, {
    loginPassword,
    loginUrl: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || 'https://app.bodyandmindon.cz',
    existingAccount,
    loginUnavailable: payload.user_id == null,
  });
  ```

Řádky 12–13 v `generatePlan.js` jsou součástí řetězce `SYS` (prompt), ne export jiné signatury. Žádné konfliktní signatury ani použití `arguments[1]` v repu nejsou.

---

## Bug 2 – Placeholder credentials v Supabase klientovi

**Stav:** Opraveno.

- **`lib/supabaseClient.js`**  
  - Placeholdery jsou konstanty `PLACEHOLDER_URL` a `PLACEHOLDER_KEY`.  
  - `isPlaceholder` se nastaví podle toho, zda se tyto hodnoty reálně používají.  
  - Při placeholderu se volá **`console.error`** v produkci (ř. 14–15) s jasnou zprávou o chybějících env proměnných.  
  - Exportuje se **`isSupabaseConfigured()`** (ř. 24–26), která vrací `false`, když běžíme s placeholdery.

Placeholdery zůstávají kvůli buildu (např. na Vercelu bez env), ale při chybějící konfiguraci je v produkci hlasitý error v logu a konfiguraci lze detekovat přes `isSupabaseConfigured()`.

options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1string\n\nOption 2Array \n\nOption 3Array \n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nOn array columnsOn range columns\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('issues')3  .select('title')4  .overlaps('tags', ['is:closed', 'severity:high'])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Match a string\n\n&#96;textSearch(column, query, options?)&#96;\n\n- For more information, see [Postgres full text search](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/full-text-search).\n\n### Parameters\n\ncolumnOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1ColumnName\n\nOption 2string\n\nquerystring\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nText searchBasic normalizationFull normalizationWebsearch\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const result = await supabase2  .from(\"texts\")3  .select(\"content\")4  .textSearch(\"content\", &#96;'eggs' &amp; 'ham'&#96;, {5    config: \"english\",6  });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Match an associated value\n\n&#96;match(query)&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nqueryOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1Record \n\nOption 2Record \n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('name')4  .match({ id: 2, name: 'Leia' })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Don't match the filter\n\n&#96;not(column, operator, value)&#96;\n\nnot() expects you to use the raw PostgREST syntax for the filter values.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1.not('id', 'in', '(5,6,7)')  // Use &#96;()&#96; for &#96;in&#96; filter2.not('arraycol', 'cs', '{\"a\",\"b\"}')  // Use &#96;cs&#96; for &#96;contains()&#96;, &#96;{}&#96; for array values\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\ncolumnOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1ColumnName\n\nOption 2string\n\noperatorOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1FilterOperator\n\nOption 2string\n\nvalueOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1Row['ColumnName']\n\nOption 2unknown\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('countries')3  .select()4  .not('name', 'is', null)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Match at least one filter\n\n&#96;or(filters, options)&#96;\n\nMatch only rows which satisfy at least one of the filters.\n\nUnlike most filters,&#96;filters&#96; is used as-is and needs to follow [PostgREST syntax](https://postgrest.org/en/stable/api.html#operators). You also need to make sure it's properly sanitized.\n\nIt's currently not possible to do an&#96;.or()&#96; filter across multiple tables.\n\nor() expects you to use the raw PostgREST syntax for the filter names and values.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1.or('id.in.(5,6,7), arraycol.cs.{\"a\",\"b\"}')  // Use &#96;()&#96; for &#96;in&#96; filter, &#96;{}&#96; for array values and &#96;cs&#96; for &#96;contains()&#96;.2.or('id.in.(5,6,7), arraycol.cd.{\"a\",\"b\"}')  // Use &#96;cd&#96; for &#96;containedBy()&#96;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nfiltersstring\n\nThe filters to use, following PostgREST syntax\n\noptionsobject\n\nNamed parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;Use &#96;or&#96; with &#96;and&#96;Use &#96;or&#96; on referenced tables\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('name')4  .or('id.eq.2,name.eq.Han')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Match the filter\n\n&#96;filter(column, operator, value)&#96;\n\nfilter() expects you to use the raw PostgREST syntax for the filter values.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1.filter('id', 'in', '(5,6,7)')  // Use &#96;()&#96; for &#96;in&#96; filter2.filter('arraycol', 'cs', '{\"a\",\"b\"}')  // Use &#96;cs&#96; for &#96;contains()&#96;, &#96;{}&#96; for array values\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\ncolumnOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1ColumnName\n\nOption 2string\n\noperatorOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1FilterOperator\n\nOption 2\"not.match\"\n\nOption 3\"not.eq\"\n\nOption 4\"not.neq\"\n\nOption 5\"not.gt\"\n\nOption 6\"not.gte\"\n\nOption 7\"not.lt\"\n\nOption 8\"not.lte\"\n\nOption 9\"not.like\"\n\nOption 10\"not.ilike\"\n\nOption 11\"not.is\"\n\nOption 12\"not.isdistinct\"\n\nOption 13\"not.in\"\n\nOption 14\"not.cs\"\n\nOption 15\"not.cd\"\n\nOption 16\"not.sl\"\n\nOption 17\"not.sr\"\n\nOption 18\"not.nxl\"\n\nOption 19\"not.nxr\"\n\nOption 20\"not.adj\"\n\nOption 21\"not.ov\"\n\nOption 22\"not.fts\"\n\nOption 23\"not.plfts\"\n\nOption 24\"not.phfts\"\n\nOption 25\"not.wfts\"\n\nOption 26\"not.imatch\"\n\nOption 27string\n\nvalueunknown\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;On a referenced table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select()4  .filter('name', 'in', '(\"Han\",\"Yoda\")')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Using modifiers\n\nFilters work on the row level—they allow you to return rows that only match certain conditions without changing the shape of the rows. Modifiers are everything that don't fit that definition—allowing you to change the format of the response (e.g., returning a CSV string).\n\nModifiers must be specified after filters. Some modifiers only apply for queries that return rows (e.g.,&#96;select()&#96; or&#96;rpc()&#96; on a function that returns a table response).\n\n---\n\n## Return data after inserting\n\n&#96;select(columns?)&#96;\n\nPerform a SELECT on the query result.\n\nBy default,&#96;.insert()&#96;,&#96;.update()&#96;,&#96;.upsert()&#96;, and&#96;.delete()&#96; do not return modified rows. By calling this method, modified rows are returned in&#96;data&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncolumns\n\nOptional\n\nQuery\n\nThe columns to retrieve, separated by commas\n\nWith &#96;upsert()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .upsert({ id: 1, name: 'Han Solo' })4  .select()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Order the results\n\n&#96;order(column, options?)&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\ncolumnOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1ColumnName\n\nOption 2string\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;On a referenced tableOrder parent table by a referenced table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('id, name')4  .order('id', { ascending: false })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Limit the number of rows returned\n\n&#96;limit(count, options)&#96;\n\nLimit the query result by&#96;count&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncountnumber\n\nThe maximum number of rows to return\n\noptionsobject\n\nNamed parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;On a referenced table\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('name')4  .limit(1)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Limit the query to a range\n\n&#96;range(from, to, options)&#96;\n\nLimit the query result by starting at an offset&#96;from&#96; and ending at the offset&#96;to&#96;. Only records within this range are returned. This respects the query order and if there is no order clause the range could behave unexpectedly. The&#96;from&#96; and&#96;to&#96; values are 0-based and inclusive:&#96;range(1, 3)&#96; will include the second, third and fourth rows of the query.\n\n### Parameters\n\nfromnumber\n\nThe starting index from which to limit the result\n\ntonumber\n\nThe last index to which to limit the result\n\noptionsobject\n\nNamed parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('name')4  .range(0, 1)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Set an abort signal\n\n&#96;abortSignal(signal)&#96;\n\nSet the AbortSignal for the fetch request.\n\nYou can use this to set a timeout for the request.\n\n### Parameters\n\nsignalAbortSignal\n\nThe AbortSignal to use for the fetch request\n\n### Return Type\n\nthis\n\nAborting requests in-flightSet a timeout\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const ac = new AbortController()2ac.abort()3const { data, error } = await supabase4  .from('very_big_table')5  .select()6  .abortSignal(ac.signal)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve one row of data\n\n&#96;single()&#96;\n\nReturn&#96;data&#96; as a single object instead of an array of objects.\n\nQuery result must be one row (e.g. using&#96;.limit(1)&#96;), otherwise this returns an error.\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select('name')4  .limit(1)5  .single()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve zero or one row of data\n\n&#96;maybeSingle()&#96;\n\nReturn&#96;data&#96; as a single object instead of an array of objects.\n\nQuery result must be zero or one row (e.g. using&#96;.limit(1)&#96;), otherwise this returns an error.\n\nWith &#96;select()&#96;\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select()4  .eq('name', 'Katniss')5  .maybeSingle()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve as a CSV\n\n&#96;csv()&#96;\n\nReturn&#96;data&#96; as a string in CSV format.\n\nReturn data as CSV\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select()4  .csv()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Override type of successful response\n\n&#96;returns()&#96;\n\nOverride the type of the returned&#96;data&#96;.\n\n- Deprecated: use overrideTypes method instead\n\nOverride type of successful responseOverride type of object response\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data } = await supabase2  .from('countries')3  .select()4  .returns&lt;Array&lt;MyType&gt;&gt;()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Partially override or replace type of successful response\n\n&#96;overrideTypes()&#96;\n\nOverride the type of the returned&#96;data&#96; field in the response.\n\nComplete Override type of successful responseComplete Override type of object responsePartial Override type of successful responsePartial Override type of object responseExample 5\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data } = await supabase2  .from('countries')3  .select()4  .overrideTypes&lt;Array&lt;MyType&gt;, { merge: false }&gt;()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Using explain\n\n&#96;explain(options)&#96;\n\nReturn&#96;data&#96; as the EXPLAIN plan for the query.\n\nYou need to enable the [db_plan_enabled](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/database/debugging-performance#enabling-explain) setting before using this method.\n\n### Parameters\n\noptionsobject\n\nNamed parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1PostgrestBuilder\n\nOption 2PostgrestBuilder\n\nGet the execution planGet the execution plan with analyze and verbose\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase2  .from('characters')3  .select()4  .explain()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nData source\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Overview\n\nThe auth methods can be accessed via the&#96;supabase.auth&#96; namespace.\n\nBy default, the supabase client sets&#96;persistSession&#96; to true and attempts to store the session in local storage. When using the supabase client in an environment that doesn't support local storage, you might notice the following warning message being logged:\n\nNo storage option exists to persist the session, which may result in unexpected behavior when using auth. If you want to set&#96;persistSession&#96; to true, please provide a storage option or you may set&#96;persistSession&#96; to false to disable this warning.\n\nThis warning message can be safely ignored if you're not using auth on the server-side. If you are using auth and you want to set&#96;persistSession&#96; to true, you will need to provide a custom storage implementation that follows [this interface](https://github.com/supabase/supabase-js/blob/master/packages/core/auth-js/src/lib/types.ts#L1053).\n\nAny email links and one-time passwords (OTPs) sent have a default expiry of 24 hours. We have the following [rate limits](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/platform/going-into-prod#auth-rate-limits) in place to guard against brute force attacks.\n\nThe expiry of an access token can be set in the \"JWT expiry limit\" field in [your project's auth settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers). A refresh token never expires and can only be used once.\n\nCreate auth clientCreate auth client (server-side)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'23const supabase = createClient(supabase_url, anon_key)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Create a new user\n\n&#96;signUp(credentials)&#96;\n\nCreates a new user.\n\nBe aware that if a user account exists in the system you may get back an error message that attempts to hide this information from the user. This method has support for PKCE via email signups. The PKCE flow cannot be used when autoconfirm is enabled.\n\nConfirm email determines if users need to confirm their email address after signing up.\n\n- If Confirm email is disabled, both a&#96;user&#96; and a&#96;session&#96; are returned.\n- If Confirm email is enabled, a&#96;user&#96; is returned but&#96;session&#96; is null.\n\nIf signUp() is called for an existing confirmed user:\n\n- When either Confirm email or Confirm phone (even when phone provider is disabled) is disabled, the error message,&#96;User already registered&#96; is returned.\n- When both Confirm email and Confirm phone (even when phone provider is disabled) are enabled in [your project](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers), an obfuscated/fake user object is returned.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignUpWithPasswordCredentials\n\n- To fetch the currently logged-in user, refer to [getUser()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-getuser).\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign up with an email and passwordSign up with a phone number and password (SMS)Sign up with a phone number and password (whatsapp)Sign up with additional user metadataSign up with a redirect URL\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signUp({2  email: 'example@email.com',3  password: 'example-password',4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Listen to auth events\n\n&#96;onAuthStateChange(callback)&#96;\n\nReceive a notification every time an auth event happens. Safe to use without an async function as callback.\n\nImportant: A callback can be an&#96;async&#96; function and it runs synchronously during the processing of the changes causing the event. You can easily create a dead-lock by using&#96;await&#96; on a call to another method of the Supabase library.\n\nDo not use other Supabase functions in the callback function. If you must, dispatch the functions once the callback has finished executing. Use this as a quick way to achieve this:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) =&gt; {2  setTimeout(async () =&gt; {3    // await on other Supabase function here4    // this runs right after the callback has finished5  }, 0)6})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- Limit the number of&#96;await&#96; calls in&#96;async&#96; callbacks.\n- Avoid using&#96;async&#96; functions as callbacks.\n\nEmitted events:\n\n&#96;INITIAL_SESSION&#96;\n\n- Emitted right after the Supabase client is constructed and the initial session from storage is loaded.\n\n&#96;SIGNED_IN&#96;\n\n- This event can fire very frequently depending on the number of tabs open in your application.\n- Avoid making assumptions as to when this event is fired, this may occur even when the user is already signed in. Instead, check the user object attached to the event to see if a new user has signed in and update your application's UI.\n- Emitted each time a user session is confirmed or re-established, including on user sign in and when refocusing a tab.\n\n&#96;SIGNED_OUT&#96;\n\nEmitted when the user signs out. This can be after:\n\nAfter the user's session has expired for any reason:\n\n- Check the [User Sessions](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions) docs for more information.\n- User has signed in on another device with single session per user enabled.\n- The session has reached its timebox limit or inactivity timeout.\n- User has signed out on another device.\n\n&#96;TOKEN_REFRESHED&#96;\n\nIt's best practice and highly recommended to extract the access token (JWT) and store it in memory for further use in your application.\n\n- Avoid frequent calls to&#96;supabase.auth.getSession()&#96; for the same purpose.\n\n&#96;USER_UPDATED&#96;\n\n- Emitted each time the&#96;supabase.auth.updateUser()&#96; method finishes successfully. Listen to it to update your application's UI based on new profile information.\n\n&#96;PASSWORD_RECOVERY&#96;\n\n- Use it to show a UI to the user where they can [reset their password](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/passwords#resetting-a-users-password-forgot-password).\n- Emitted instead of the&#96;SIGNED_IN&#96; event when the user lands on a page that includes a password recovery link in the URL.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncallbackfunction\n\nA callback function to be invoked when an auth event happens.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nobject\n\nDetails\n\nListen to auth changesListen to sign outStore OAuth provider tokens on sign inUse React Context for the User's sessionListen to password recovery eventsListen to sign inListen to token refreshListen to user updates\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data } = supabase.auth.onAuthStateChange((event, session) =&gt; {2  console.log(event, session)34  if (event === 'INITIAL_SESSION') {5    // handle initial session6  } else if (event === 'SIGNED_IN') {7    // handle sign in event8  } else if (event === 'SIGNED_OUT') {9    // handle sign out event10  } else if (event === 'PASSWORD_RECOVERY') {11    // handle password recovery event12  } else if (event === 'TOKEN_REFRESHED') {13    // handle token refreshed event14  } else if (event === 'USER_UPDATED') {15    // handle user updated event16  }17})1819// call unsubscribe to remove the callback20data.subscription.unsubscribe()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Create an anonymous user\n\n&#96;signInAnonymously(credentials?)&#96;\n\nCreates a new anonymous user.\n\n- It is recommended to set up captcha for anonymous sign-ins to prevent abuse. You can pass in the captcha token in the&#96;options&#96; param.\n- Returns an anonymous user\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentials\n\nOptional\n\nSignInAnonymouslyCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate an anonymous userCreate an anonymous user with custom user metadata\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInAnonymously({2  options: {3    captchaToken4  }5});\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user\n\n&#96;signInWithPassword(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user with an email and password or phone and password.\n\nBe aware that you may get back an error message that will not distinguish between the cases where the account does not exist or that the email/phone and password combination is wrong or that the account can only be accessed via social login.\n\n- Requires either an email and password or a phone number and password.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithPasswordCredentials\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with email and passwordSign in with phone and password\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithPassword({2  email: 'example@email.com',3  password: 'example-password',4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in with ID token (native sign-in)\n\n&#96;signInWithIdToken(credentials)&#96;\n\nAllows signing in with an OIDC ID token. The authentication provider used should be enabled and configured.\n\n- You can also use Google's [One Tap](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/display-google-one-tap) and [Automatic sign-in](https://developers.google.com/identity/gsi/web/guides/automatic-sign-in-sign-out) via this API.\n- Especially useful when implementing sign in using native platform dialogs in mobile or desktop apps using Sign in with Apple or Sign in with Google on iOS and Android.\n- Use an ID token to sign in.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithIdTokenCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign In using ID Token\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithIdToken({2  provider: 'google',3  token: 'your-id-token'4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through OTP\n\n&#96;signInWithOtp(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in a user using magiclink or a one-time password (OTP).\n\nIf the&#96;{{ .ConfirmationURL }}&#96; variable is specified in the email template, a magiclink will be sent. If the&#96;{{ .Token }}&#96; variable is specified in the email template, an OTP will be sent. If you're using phone sign-ins, only an OTP will be sent. You won't be able to send a magiclink for phone sign-ins.\n\nBe aware that you may get back an error message that will not distinguish between the cases where the account does not exist or, that the account can only be accessed via social login.\n\nDo note that you will need to configure a Whatsapp sender on Twilio if you are using phone sign in with the 'whatsapp' channel. The whatsapp channel is not supported on other providers at this time. This method supports PKCE when an email is passed.\n\n- See our [Twilio Phone Auth Guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/phone-login?showSMSProvider=Twilio) for details about configuring WhatsApp sign in.\n- Magic links and OTPs share the same implementation. To send users a one-time code instead of a magic link, [modify the magic link email template](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/templates) to include&#96;{{ .Token }}&#96; instead of&#96;{{ .ConfirmationURL }}&#96;.\n- See [redirect URLs and wildcards](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls) to add additional redirect URLs to your project.\n- The magic link's destination URL is determined by the [SITE_URL](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls).\n- If you're using phone, you can configure whether you want the user to receive a OTP.\n- If you're using an email, you can configure whether you want the user to receive a magiclink or a OTP.\n- If the user doesn't exist,&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; will signup the user instead. To restrict this behavior, you can set&#96;shouldCreateUser&#96; in&#96;SignInWithPasswordlessCredentials.options&#96; to&#96;false&#96;.\n- This method is used for passwordless sign-ins where a OTP is sent to the user's email or phone number.\n- Requires either an email or phone number.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with emailSign in with SMS OTPSign in with WhatsApp OTP\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOtp({2  email: 'example@email.com',3  options: {4    emailRedirectTo: 'https://example.com/welcome'5  }6})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through OAuth\n\n&#96;signInWithOAuth(credentials)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user via a third-party provider. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- It works by redirecting your application to the provider's authorization screen, before bringing back the user to your app.\n- This method is used for signing in using [Social Login (OAuth) providers](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth#configure-third-party-providers).\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsSignInWithOAuthCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in using a third-party providerSign in using a third-party provider with redirectSign in with scopes and access provider tokens\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithOAuth({2  provider: 'github'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through SSO\n\n&#96;signInWithSSO(params)&#96;\n\nAttempts a single-sign on using an enterprise Identity Provider. A successful SSO attempt will redirect the current page to the identity provider authorization page. The redirect URL is implementation and SSO protocol specific.\n\nYou can use it by providing a SSO domain. Typically you can extract this domain by asking users for their email address. If this domain is registered on the Auth instance the redirect will use that organization's currently active SSO Identity Provider for the login.\n\nIf you have built an organization-specific login page, you can use the organization's SSO Identity Provider UUID directly instead.\n\nIn case you need to use a different way to start the authentication flow with an identity provider, you can use the&#96;providerId&#96; property. For example:\n\n- Using different hints to identity the identity provider to be used by the user, like a company-specific page, IP address or other tracking information.\n- Mapping specific user email addresses with an identity provider.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with email domainSign in with provider UUID\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// You can extract the user's email domain and use it to trigger the2  // authentication flow with the correct identity provider.34  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithSSO({5    domain: 'company.com'6  })78  if (data?.url) {9    // redirect the user to the identity provider's authentication flow10    window.location.href = data.url11  }\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Sign in a user through Web3 (Solana, Ethereum)\n\n&#96;signInWithWeb3(credentials)&#96;\n\nSigns in a user by verifying a message signed by the user's private key. Supports Ethereum (via Sign-In-With-Ethereum) &amp; Solana (Sign-In-With-Solana) standards, both of which derive from the EIP-4361 standard With slight variation on Solana's side.\n\n- Read up on the [potential for abuse](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-web3#potential-for-abuse) before using it.\n- Uses a Web3 (Ethereum, Solana) wallet to sign a user in.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1One of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2One of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSign in with Solana or Ethereum (Window API)Sign in with Ethereum (Message and Signature)Sign in with Solana (Brave)Sign in with Solana (Wallet Adapter)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// uses window.ethereum for the wallet2  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithWeb3({3    chain: 'ethereum',4    statement: 'I accept the Terms of Service at https://example.com/tos'5  })67  // uses window.solana for the wallet8  const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.signInWithWeb3({9    chain: 'solana',10    statement: 'I accept the Terms of Service at https://example.com/tos'11  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Get user claims from verified JWT\n\n&#96;getClaims(jwt?, options)&#96;\n\nExtracts the JWT claims present in the access token by first verifying the JWT against the server's JSON Web Key Set endpoint&#96;/.well-known/jwks.json&#96; which is often cached, resulting in significantly faster responses. Prefer this method over #getUser which always sends a request to the Auth server for each JWT.\n\nIf the project is not using an asymmetric JWT signing key (like ECC or RSA) it always sends a request to the Auth server (similar to #getUser) to verify the JWT.\n\n- The returned claims can be customized per project using the [Custom Access Token Hook](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-hooks/custom-access-token-hook).\n- If your project is using a symmetric secret to sign the JWT, it always sends a request similar to&#96;getUser()&#96; to validate the JWT at the server before returning the decoded token. This is also used if the WebCrypto API is not available in the environment. Make sure you polyfill it in such situations.\n- If the user's access token is about to expire when calling this function, the user's session will first be refreshed before validating the JWT.\n- A network request is sent to your project's JWT signing key discovery endpoint&#96;https://project-id.supabase.co/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json&#96;, which is cached locally. If your environment is ephemeral, such as a Lambda function that is destroyed after every request, a network request will be sent for each new invocation. Supabase provides a network-edge cache providing fast responses for these situations.\n- If your project is using asymmetric JWT signing keys, then the verification is done locally usually without a network request using the [WebCrypto API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Web_Crypto_API).\n- Parses the user's [access token](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions#access-token-jwt-claims) as a [JSON Web Token (JWT)](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/jwts) and returns its components if valid and not expired.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nAn optional specific JWT you wish to verify, not the one you can obtain from #getSession.\n\noptionsobject\n\nVarious additional options that allow you to customize the behavior of this method.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nGet JWT claims, header and signature\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getClaims()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign out a user\n\n&#96;signOut(options)&#96;\n\nInside a browser context,&#96;signOut()&#96; will remove the logged in user from the browser session and log them out - removing all items from localstorage and then trigger a&#96;\"SIGNED_OUT\"&#96; event.\n\nFor server-side management, you can revoke all refresh tokens for a user by passing a user's JWT through to&#96;auth.api.signOut(JWT: string)&#96;. There is no way to revoke a user's access token jwt until it expires. It is recommended to set a shorter expiry on the jwt for this reason.\n\nIf using&#96;others&#96; scope, no&#96;SIGNED_OUT&#96; event is fired!\n\n- Since Supabase Auth uses JWTs for authentication, the access token JWT will be valid until it's expired. When the user signs out, Supabase revokes the refresh token and deletes the JWT from the client-side. This does not revoke the JWT and it will still be valid until it expires.\n- By default,&#96;signOut()&#96; uses the global scope, which signs out all other sessions that the user is logged into as well. Customize this behavior by passing a scope parameter.\n- In order to use the&#96;signOut()&#96; method, the user needs to be signed in first.\n\n### Parameters\n\noptionsSignOut\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nSign out (all sessions)Sign out (current session)Sign out (other sessions)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.signOut()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Send a password reset request\n\n&#96;resetPasswordForEmail(email, options)&#96;\n\nSends a password reset request to an email address. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- After the user has been redirected successfully, prompt them for a new password and call&#96;updateUser()&#96;:\n- When the user clicks the reset link in the email they are redirected back to your application. You can configure the URL that the user is redirected to with the&#96;redirectTo&#96; parameter. See [redirect URLs and wildcards](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/redirect-urls#use-wildcards-in-redirect-urls) to add additional redirect URLs to your project.\n- A&#96;PASSWORD_RECOVERY&#96; event will be emitted when the password recovery link is clicked. You can use [onAuthStateChange()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-onauthstatechange) to listen and invoke a callback function on these events.\n- The&#96;resetPasswordForEmail()&#96; only sends a password reset link to the user's email. To update the user's password, see [updateUser()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-updateuser).\n- The password reset flow consist of 2 broad steps: (i) Allow the user to login via the password reset link; (ii) Update the user's password.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({2  password: new_password3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nemailstring\n\nThe email address of the user.\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nReset passwordReset password (React)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.resetPasswordForEmail(email, {2  redirectTo: 'https://example.com/update-password',3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Verify and log in through OTP\n\n&#96;verifyOtp(params)&#96;\n\nLog in a user given a User supplied OTP or TokenHash received through mobile or email.\n\nIf a phone number is used, the type can either be:\n\n1. &#96;phone_change&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to a new phone number during a phone number update process.\n2. &#96;sms&#96;– Used when verifying a one-time password (OTP) sent via SMS during sign-up or sign-in.\n\nIf an email address is used, the type can be one of the following (note:&#96;signup&#96; and&#96;magiclink&#96; types are deprecated):\n\n1. &#96;email_change&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to a new email address during an email update process.\n2. &#96;invite&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent as part of an invitation to join a project or organization.\n3. &#96;recovery&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent for account recovery, typically after a password reset request.\n4. &#96;email&#96;– Used when verifying an OTP sent to the user's email during sign-up or sign-in.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1VerifyMobileOtpParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2VerifyEmailOtpParams\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3VerifyTokenHashParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nVerify Signup One-Time Password (OTP)Verify SMS One-Time Password (OTP)Verify Email Auth (Token Hash)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.verifyOtp({ email, token, type: 'email'})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a session\n\n&#96;getSession()&#96;\n\nReturns the session, refreshing it if necessary.\n\nThe session returned can be null if the session is not detected which can happen in the event a user is not signed-in or has logged out.\n\nIMPORTANT: This method loads values directly from the storage attached to the client. If that storage is based on request cookies for example, the values in it may not be authentic and therefore it's strongly advised against using this method and its results in such circumstances. A warning will be emitted if this is detected. Use #getUser() instead.\n\n- When using in a browser, this function is synchronized across all tabs using the [LockManager](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/LockManager) API. In other environments make sure you've defined a proper&#96;lock&#96; property, if necessary, to make sure there are no race conditions while the session is being refreshed.\n- IMPORTANT SECURITY NOTICE: If using an insecure storage medium, such as cookies or request headers, the user object returned by this function must not be trusted. Always verify the JWT using&#96;getClaims()&#96; or your own JWT verification library to securely establish the user's identity and access. You can also use&#96;getUser()&#96; to fetch the user object directly from the Auth server for this purpose.\n- When using in a browser, or you've called&#96;startAutoRefresh()&#96; in your environment (React Native, etc.) this function always returns a valid access token without refreshing the session itself, as this is done in the background. This function returns very fast.\n- If the session's access token is expired or is about to expire, this method will use the refresh token to refresh the session.\n- The session contains an access token (signed JWT), a refresh token and the user object.\n- Retrieves the current [user session](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/sessions) from the storage medium (local storage, cookies).\n- Since the introduction of [asymmetric JWT signing keys](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/signing-keys), this method is considered low-level and we encourage you to use&#96;getClaims()&#96; or&#96;getUser()&#96; instead.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the session data\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getSession()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a new session\n\n&#96;refreshSession(currentSession?)&#96;\n\nReturns a new session, regardless of expiry status. Takes in an optional current session. If not passed in, then refreshSession() will attempt to retrieve it from getSession(). If the current session's refresh token is invalid, an error will be thrown.\n\n- This method will refresh and return a new session whether the current one is expired or not.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncurrentSession\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nThe current session. If passed in, it must contain a refresh token.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nRefresh session using the current sessionRefresh session using a refresh token\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.refreshSession()2const { session, user } = data\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a user\n\n&#96;getUser(jwt?)&#96;\n\nGets the current user details if there is an existing session. This method performs a network request to the Supabase Auth server, so the returned value is authentic and can be used to base authorization rules on.\n\n- Should always be used when checking for user authorization on the server. On the client, you can instead use&#96;getSession().session.user&#96; for faster results.&#96;getSession&#96; is insecure on the server.\n- This method is useful for checking if the user is authorized because it validates the user's access token JWT on the server.\n- This method fetches the user object from the database instead of local session.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nTakes in an optional access token JWT. If no JWT is provided, the JWT from the current session is used.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the logged in user with the current existing sessionGet the logged in user with a custom access token jwt\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data: { user } } = await supabase.auth.getUser()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Update a user\n\n&#96;updateUser(attributes, options)&#96;\n\nUpdates user data for a logged in user.\n\n- By default, email updates sends a confirmation link to both the user's current and new email. To only send a confirmation link to the user's new email, disable Secure email change in your project's [email auth provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- In order to use the&#96;updateUser()&#96; method, the user needs to be signed in first.\n\n### Parameters\n\nattributesUserAttributes\n\nDetails\n\noptionsobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpdate the email for an authenticated userUpdate the phone number for an authenticated userUpdate the password for an authenticated userUpdate the user's metadataUpdate the user's password with a nonce\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.updateUser({2  email: 'new@email.com'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve identities linked to a user\n\n&#96;getUserIdentities()&#96;\n\nGets all the identities linked to a user.\n\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;getUserIdentities()&#96;.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nReturns a list of identities linked to the user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.getUserIdentities()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Link an identity to a user\n\n&#96;linkIdentity(credentials)&#96;\n\nLinks an oauth identity to an existing user. This method supports the PKCE flow.\n\n- If&#96;linkIdentity&#96; is run in the browser, the user is automatically redirected to the returned URL. On the server, you should handle the redirect.\n- If the candidate identity is already linked to the existing user or another user,&#96;linkIdentity()&#96; will fail.\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;linkIdentity()&#96;.\n- The Enable Manual Linking option must be enabled from your [project's authentication settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1SignInWithOAuthCredentials\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2SignInWithIdTokenCredentials\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nLink an identity to a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.linkIdentity({2  provider: 'github'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Unlink an identity from a user\n\n&#96;unlinkIdentity(identity)&#96;\n\nUnlinks an identity from a user by deleting it. The user will no longer be able to sign in with that identity once it's unlinked.\n\n- The identity to be unlinked must belong to the user.\n- The user must have at least 2 identities in order to unlink an identity.\n- The user needs to be signed in to call&#96;unlinkIdentity()&#96;.\n- The Enable Manual Linking option must be enabled from your [project's authentication settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n\n### Parameters\n\nidentityUserIdentity\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUnlink an identity\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1// retrieve all identities linked to a user2const identities = await supabase.auth.getUserIdentities()34// find the google identity5const googleIdentity = identities.find(6  identity =&gt; identity.provider === 'google'7)89// unlink the google identity10const { error } = await supabase.auth.unlinkIdentity(googleIdentity)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Send a password reauthentication nonce\n\n&#96;reauthenticate()&#96;\n\nSends a reauthentication OTP to the user's email or phone number. Requires the user to be signed-in.\n\n- After receiving the OTP, include it as the&#96;nonce&#96; in your&#96;updateUser()&#96; call to finalize the password change.\n- This method will send a nonce to the user's email. If the user doesn't have a confirmed email address, the method will send the nonce to the user's confirmed phone number instead.\n- A user is only require to reauthenticate before updating their password if Secure password change is enabled and the user hasn't recently signed in. A user is deemed recently signed in if the session was created in the last 24 hours.\n- If you require your user to reauthenticate before updating their password, you need to enable the Secure password change option in your [project's email provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- This method is used together with&#96;updateUser()&#96; when a user's password needs to be updated.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSend reauthentication nonce\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.reauthenticate()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Resend an OTP\n\n&#96;resend(credentials)&#96;\n\nResends an existing signup confirmation email, email change email, SMS OTP or phone change OTP.\n\n- You can specify a redirect url when you resend an email link using the&#96;emailRedirectTo&#96; option.\n- This method will only resend an email or phone OTP to the user if there was an initial signup, email change or phone change request being made(note: For existing users signing in with OTP, you should use&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; again to resend the OTP).\n- Password recovery emails can be resent by calling the&#96;resetPasswordForEmail()&#96; method again.\n- Passwordless sign-ins can be resent by calling the&#96;signInWithOtp()&#96; method again.\n- Resends a signup confirmation, email change or phone change email to the user.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncredentialsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nResend an email signup confirmationResend a phone signup confirmationResend email change emailResend phone change OTP\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { error } = await supabase.auth.resend({2  type: 'signup',3  email: 'email@example.com',4  options: {5    emailRedirectTo: 'https://example.com/welcome'6  }7})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Set the session data\n\n&#96;setSession(currentSession)&#96;\n\nSets the session data from the current session. If the current session is expired, setSession will take care of refreshing it to obtain a new session. If the refresh token or access token in the current session is invalid, an error will be thrown.\n\n- If successful, a&#96;SIGNED_IN&#96; event is emitted.\n- This method sets the session using an&#96;access_token&#96; and&#96;refresh_token&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\ncurrentSessionobject\n\nThe current session that minimally contains an access token and refresh token.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nSet the session\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.setSession({2    access_token,3    refresh_token4  })\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\nNotes\n\n---\n\n## Exchange an auth code for a session\n\n&#96;exchangeCodeForSession(authCode)&#96;\n\nLog in an existing user by exchanging an Auth Code issued during the PKCE flow.\n\n- Used when&#96;flowType&#96; is set to&#96;pkce&#96; in client options.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthCodestring\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nExchange Auth Code\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1supabase.auth.exchangeCodeForSession('34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Start auto-refresh session (non-browser)\n\n&#96;startAutoRefresh()&#96;\n\nStarts an auto-refresh process in the background. The session is checked every few seconds. Close to the time of expiration a process is started to refresh the session. If refreshing fails it will be retried for as long as necessary.\n\nIf you set the GoTrueClientOptions#autoRefreshToken you don't need to call this function, it will be called for you.\n\nOn browsers the refresh process works only when the tab/window is in the foreground to conserve resources as well as prevent race conditions and flooding auth with requests. If you call this method any managed visibility change callback will be removed and you must manage visibility changes on your own.\n\nOn non-browser platforms the refresh process works continuously in the background, which may not be desirable. You should hook into your platform's foreground indication mechanism and call these methods appropriately to conserve resources.\n\n#stopAutoRefresh\n\n- To give this hint to the application, you should be calling this method when the app is in focus and calling&#96;supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()&#96; when it's out of focus.\n- On non-browser platforms, such as mobile or desktop apps built with web technologies, the library is not able to effectively determine whether the application is focused or not.\n- The Supabase Auth library automatically starts and stops proactively refreshing the session when a tab is focused or not.\n- Only useful in non-browser environments such as React Native or Electron.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nStart and stop auto refresh in React Native\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { AppState } from 'react-native'23// make sure you register this only once!4AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) =&gt; {5  if (state === 'active') {6    supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh()7  } else {8    supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()9  }10})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Stop auto-refresh session (non-browser)\n\n&#96;stopAutoRefresh()&#96;\n\nStops an active auto refresh process running in the background (if any).\n\nIf you call this method any managed visibility change callback will be removed and you must manage visibility changes on your own.\n\nSee #startAutoRefresh for more details.\n\n- When your application goes in the background or out of focus, call this method to stop the proactive refreshing of the session.\n- On non-browser platforms, such as mobile or desktop apps built with web technologies, the library is not able to effectively determine whether the application is focused or not.\n- The Supabase Auth library automatically starts and stops proactively refreshing the session when a tab is focused or not.\n- Only useful in non-browser environments such as React Native or Electron.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nStart and stop auto refresh in React Native\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { AppState } from 'react-native'23// make sure you register this only once!4AppState.addEventListener('change', (state) =&gt; {5  if (state === 'active') {6    supabase.auth.startAutoRefresh()7  } else {8    supabase.auth.stopAutoRefresh()9  }10})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Initialize client session\n\n&#96;initialize()&#96;\n\nInitializes the client session either from the url or from storage. This method is automatically called when instantiating the client, but should also be called manually when checking for an error from an auth redirect (oauth, magiclink, password recovery, etc).\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Auth MFA\n\nThis section contains methods commonly used for Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) and are invoked behind the&#96;supabase.auth.mfa&#96; namespace.\n\nCurrently, there is support for time-based one-time password (TOTP) and phone verification code as the 2nd factor. Recovery codes are not supported but users can enroll multiple factors, with an upper limit of 10.\n\nHaving a 2nd factor for recovery frees the user of the burden of having to store their recovery codes somewhere. It also reduces the attack surface since multiple recovery codes are usually generated compared to just having 1 backup factor.\n\nLearn more about implementing MFA in your application [in the MFA guide](https://supabase.com/docs/guides/auth/auth-mfa#overview).\n\n---\n\n## Enroll a factor\n\n&#96;enroll(params)&#96;\n\nStarts the enrollment process for a new Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) factor. This method creates a new&#96;unverified&#96; factor. To verify a factor, present the QR code or secret to the user and ask them to add it to their authenticator app. The user has to enter the code from their authenticator app to verify it.\n\nUpon verifying a factor, all other sessions are logged out and the current session's authenticator level is promoted to&#96;aal2&#96;.\n\n- To generate a QR code for the&#96;totp&#96; secret in Next.js, you can do the following:\n- To create and verify a TOTP challenge in a single step, see [mfa.challengeAndVerify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challengeandverify).\n- To verify a challenge, see [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify).\n- To create a challenge, see [mfa.challenge()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge).\n- Use&#96;totp&#96; or&#96;phone&#96; as the&#96;factorType&#96; and use the returned&#96;id&#96; to create a challenge.\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1&lt;Image src={data.totp.qr_code} alt={data.totp.uri} layout=\"fill\"&gt;&lt;/Image&gt;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n- The&#96;challenge&#96; and&#96;verify&#96; steps are separated when using Phone factors as the user will need time to receive and input the code obtained from the SMS in challenge.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 4MFAEnrollTOTPParams\n\nOption 5MFAEnrollPhoneParams\n\nOption 6MFAEnrollWebauthnParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nEnroll a time-based, one-time password (TOTP) factorEnroll a Phone Factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.enroll({2  factorType: 'totp',3  friendlyName: 'your_friendly_name'4})56// Use the id to create a challenge.7// The challenge can be verified by entering the code generated from the authenticator app.8// The code will be generated upon scanning the qr_code or entering the secret into the authenticator app.9const { id, type, totp: { qr_code, secret, uri }, friendly_name } = data10const challenge = await supabase.auth.mfa.challenge({ factorId: id });\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create a challenge\n\n&#96;challenge(params)&#96;\n\nPrepares a challenge used to verify that a user has access to a MFA factor.\n\n- A phone factor sends a code to the user upon challenge. The channel defaults to&#96;sms&#96; unless otherwise specified.\n- To verify a challenge, see [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify).\n- An [enrolled factor](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-enroll) is required before creating a challenge.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 4MFAChallengeTOTPParams\n\nOption 5MFAChallengePhoneParams\n\nOption 6MFAChallengeWebauthnParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate a challenge for a factorCreate a challenge for a phone factorCreate a challenge for a phone factor (WhatsApp)\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challenge({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225'3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Verify a challenge\n\n&#96;verify(params)&#96;\n\nVerifies a code against a challenge. The verification code is provided by the user by entering a code seen in their authenticator app.\n\n- To verify a challenge, please [create a challenge](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge) first.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsOne of the following options\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 3MFAVerifyTOTPParams\n\nOption 4MFAVerifyPhoneParams\n\nOption 5MFAVerifyWebauthnParams\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nVerify a challenge for a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.verify({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  challengeId: '4034ae6f-a8ce-4fb5-8ee5-69a5863a7c15',4  code: '123456'5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Create and verify a challenge\n\n&#96;challengeAndVerify(params)&#96;\n\nHelper method which creates a challenge and immediately uses the given code to verify against it thereafter. The verification code is provided by the user by entering a code seen in their authenticator app.\n\n- Executes [mfa.challenge()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-challenge) and [mfa.verify()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-verify) in a single step.\n- An [enrolled factor](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-mfa-enroll) is required before invoking&#96;challengeAndVerify()&#96;.\n- Intended for use with only TOTP factors.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsobject\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nCreate and verify a challenge for a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.challengeAndVerify({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  code: '123456'4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Unenroll a factor\n\n&#96;unenroll(params)&#96;\n\nUnenroll removes a MFA factor. A user has to have an&#96;aal2&#96; authenticator level in order to unenroll a&#96;verified&#96; factor.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsMFAUnenrollParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUnenroll a factor\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.unenroll({2  factorId: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Get Authenticator Assurance Level\n\n&#96;getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel(jwt?)&#96;\n\nReturns the Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL) for the active session.\n\n- &#96;aal2&#96; means that the user's identity has been verified both with a conventional login and at least one MFA factor.\n- &#96;aal1&#96;(or&#96;null&#96;) means that the user's identity has been verified only with a conventional login (email+password, OTP, magic link, social login, etc.).\n\nWhen called without a JWT parameter, this method is fairly quick (microseconds) and rarely uses the network. When a JWT is provided (useful in server-side environments like Edge Functions where no session is stored), this method will make a network request to validate the user and fetch their MFA factors.\n\n- An optional&#96;jwt&#96; parameter can be passed to check the AAL level of a specific JWT instead of the current session.\n- If the user has a verified factor, the&#96;nextLevel&#96; field will return&#96;aal2&#96;, else, it will return&#96;aal1&#96;.\n- In Supabase, having an AAL of&#96;aal1&#96; refers to having the 1st factor of authentication such as an email and password or OAuth sign-in while&#96;aal2&#96; refers to the 2nd factor of authentication such as a time-based, one-time-password (TOTP) or Phone factor.\n- Authenticator Assurance Level (AAL) is the measure of the strength of an authentication mechanism.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwt\n\nOptional\n\nstring\n\nAn optional JWT to check the AAL level for. If not provided, the current session's JWT is used.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet the AAL details of a sessionGet the AAL details for a specific JWT\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.mfa.getAuthenticatorAssuranceLevel()2const { currentLevel, nextLevel, currentAuthenticationMethods } = data\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all factors for current user\n\n&#96;listFactors()&#96;\n\nReturns the list of MFA factors enabled for this user.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## OAuth Server\n\nThe OAuth Server API allows you to build custom OAuth consent screens for your application. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\n---\n\n## Get authorization details\n\n&#96;getAuthorizationDetails(authorizationId)&#96;\n\nRetrieves details about an OAuth authorization request. Used to display consent information to the user. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nThis method returns one of two response types:\n\n- &#96;OAuthRedirect&#96;: User already consented - redirect immediately to the OAuth client\n- &#96;OAuthAuthorizationDetails&#96;: User needs to consent - show consent page with client info\n\nUse type narrowing to distinguish between the responses:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1if ('authorization_id' in data) {2  // Show consent page3} else {4  // Redirect to data.redirect_url5}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID from the authorization request\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Approve authorization\n\n&#96;approveAuthorization(authorizationId, options?)&#96;\n\nApproves an OAuth authorization request. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nAfter approval, the user's consent is stored and an authorization code is generated. The response contains a complete redirect URL with the authorization code and state.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID to approve\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nOptional parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Deny authorization\n\n&#96;denyAuthorization(authorizationId, options?)&#96;\n\nDenies an OAuth authorization request. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nAfter denial, the response contains a redirect URL with an OAuth error (access_denied) to inform the OAuth client that the user rejected the request.\n\n### Parameters\n\nauthorizationIdstring\n\nThe authorization ID to deny\n\noptions\n\nOptional\n\nobject\n\nOptional parameters\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## List grants\n\n&#96;listGrants()&#96;\n\nLists all OAuth grants that the authenticated user has authorized. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Revoke grant\n\n&#96;revokeGrant(options)&#96;\n\nRevokes a user's OAuth grant for a specific client. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth.\n\nRevocation marks consent as revoked, deletes active sessions for that OAuth client, and invalidates associated refresh tokens.\n\n### Parameters\n\noptionsobject\n\nRevocation options\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Auth Admin\n\n- These methods are considered admin methods and should be called on a trusted server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n- Any method under the&#96;supabase.auth.admin&#96; namespace requires a&#96;service_role&#96; key.\n\nCreate server-side auth client\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1import { createClient } from '@supabase/supabase-js'23const supabase = createClient(supabase_url, service_role_key, {4  auth: {5    autoRefreshToken: false,6    persistSession: false7  }8})910// Access auth admin api11const adminAuthClient = supabase.auth.admin\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Retrieve a user\n\n&#96;getUserById(uid)&#96;\n\nGet user by id.\n\n- The&#96;getUserById()&#96; method requires the user's id which maps to the&#96;auth.users.id&#96; column.\n- Fetches the user object from the database based on the user's id.\n\n### Parameters\n\nuidstring\n\nThe user's unique identifier\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nFetch the user object using the access_token jwt\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.getUserById(1)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all users\n\n&#96;listUsers(params?)&#96;\n\nGet a list of users.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n- Defaults to return 50 users per page.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparams\n\nOptional\n\nPageParams\n\nAn object which supports&#96;page&#96; and&#96;perPage&#96; as numbers, to alter the paginated results.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGet a page of usersPaginated list of users\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data: { users }, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.listUsers()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n---\n\n## Create a user\n\n&#96;createUser(attributes)&#96;\n\nCreates a new user. This function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n- If you are sure that the created user's email or phone number is legitimate and verified, you can set the&#96;email_confirm&#96; or&#96;phone_confirm&#96; param to&#96;true&#96;.\n- &#96;createUser()&#96; will not send a confirmation email to the user. You can use [inviteUserByEmail()](https://supabase.com/docs/reference/javascript/auth-admin-inviteuserbyemail) if you want to send them an email invite instead.\n- To confirm the user's email address or phone number, set&#96;email_confirm&#96; or&#96;phone_confirm&#96; to true. Both arguments default to false.\n\n### Parameters\n\nattributesAdminUserAttributes\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nWith custom user metadataAuto-confirm the user's emailAuto-confirm the user's phone number\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.createUser({2  email: 'user@email.com',3  password: 'password',4  user_metadata: { name: 'Yoda' }5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Delete a user\n\n&#96;deleteUser(id, shouldSoftDelete)&#96;\n\nDelete a user. Requires a&#96;service_role&#96; key.\n\n- The&#96;deleteUser()&#96; method requires the user's ID, which maps to the&#96;auth.users.id&#96; column.\n\n### Parameters\n\nidstring\n\nThe user id you want to remove.\n\nshouldSoftDeleteboolean\n\nIf true, then the user will be soft-deleted from the auth schema. Soft deletion allows user identification from the hashed user ID but is not reversible. Defaults to false for backward compatibility.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nRemoves a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.deleteUser(2  '715ed5db-f090-4b8c-a067-640ecee36aa0'3)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Send an email invite link\n\n&#96;inviteUserByEmail(email, options)&#96;\n\nSends an invite link to an email address.\n\n- Note that PKCE is not supported when using&#96;inviteUserByEmail&#96;. This is because the browser initiating the invite is often different from the browser accepting the invite which makes it difficult to provide the security guarantees required of the PKCE flow.\n- The&#96;inviteUserByEmail()&#96; method is typically used by administrators to invite users to join the application.\n- Sends an invite link to the user's email address.\n\n### Parameters\n\nemailstring\n\nThe email address of the user.\n\noptionsobject\n\nAdditional options to be included when inviting.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nInvite a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.inviteUserByEmail('email@example.com')\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Generate an email link\n\n&#96;generateLink(params)&#96;\n\nGenerates email links and OTPs to be sent via a custom email provider.\n\n- &#96;generateLink()&#96; handles the creation of the user for&#96;signup&#96;,&#96;invite&#96; and&#96;magiclink&#96;.\n- &#96;generateLink()&#96; only generates the email link for&#96;email_change_email&#96; if the Secure email change is enabled in your project's [email auth provider settings](https://supabase.com/dashboard/project/_/auth/providers).\n- The following types can be passed into&#96;generateLink()&#96;:&#96;signup&#96;,&#96;magiclink&#96;,&#96;invite&#96;,&#96;recovery&#96;,&#96;email_change_current&#96;,&#96;email_change_new&#96;,&#96;phone_change&#96;.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsGenerateLinkParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nGenerate a signup linkGenerate an invite linkGenerate a magic linkGenerate a recovery linkGenerate links to change current email address\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.generateLink({2  type: 'signup',3  email: 'email@example.com',4  password: 'secret'5})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Update a user\n\n&#96;updateUserById(uid, attributes)&#96;\n\nUpdates the user data. Changes are applied directly without confirmation flows.\n\n### Parameters\n\nuidstring\n\nThe user's unique identifier\n\nattributesAdminUserAttributes\n\nThe data you want to update.\n\nThis function should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nUpdates a user's emailUpdates a user's passwordUpdates a user's metadataUpdates a user's app_metadataConfirms a user's email addressConfirms a user's phone numberBan a user for 100 years\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data: user, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.updateUserById(2  '11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111',3  { email: 'new@email.com' }4)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## Sign out a user (admin)\n\n&#96;signOut(jwt, scope)&#96;\n\nRemoves a logged-in session.\n\n### Parameters\n\njwtstring\n\nA valid, logged-in JWT.\n\nscopeOne of the following options\n\nThe logout sope.\n\nDetails\n\nOption 1\"global\"\n\nOption 2\"local\"\n\nOption 3\"others\"\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\n---\n\n## Delete a factor for a user\n\n&#96;deleteFactor(params)&#96;\n\nDeletes a factor on a user. This will log the user out of all active sessions if the deleted factor was verified.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsAuthMFAAdminDeleteFactorParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nDelete a factor for a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.mfa.deleteFactor({2  id: '34e770dd-9ff9-416c-87fa-43b31d7ef225',3  userId: 'a89baba7-b1b7-440f-b4bb-91026967f66b',4})\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## List all factors for a user (admin)\n\n&#96;listFactors(params)&#96;\n\nLists all factors associated to a user.\n\n### Parameters\n\nparamsAuthMFAAdminListFactorsParams\n\nDetails\n\n### Return Type\n\nPromise \n\nDetails\n\nOption 1object\n\nDetails\n\nOption 2object\n\nDetails\n\nList all factors for a user\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n1const { data, error } = await supabase.auth.admin.mfa.listFactors()\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nResponse\n\n---\n\n## OAuth Admin\n\nThe OAuth Admin API allows you to manage OAuth clients programmatically. Only relevant when the OAuth 2.1 server is enabled in Supabase Auth. These functions should only be called on a server. Never expose your&#96;service_role&#96; key in the browser.\n\n---\n\n## List OAuth clients\n\n&#96;listClients(params?)&#96;\n\nLists all OAuth clients with optional pagination.
